summary: All in src/finder. filter.rs `apply_filter_to`: `filter_source` holds for each row its path with the size and date the filter was given (`FilterInput`), where it held the path alone, so a run starts when a row comes back with another size or date as well as when the items or their order differ. mod.rs `refresh`: sets `filter_source = None`, so Refresh runs the filter again for whatever comes back. mod.rs `reload_recents`: compares by `as_listed` (path, size, modified) where it compared by path, so Recents read again in the same order with a file in it changed is shown. mod.rs `start_search`'s answer (the review's version): a quiet answer that isn't shown gives the rows on screen what it has for their items where one came back with another size or date (`show_as_found`: rows are replaced in place by path, none comes, goes or moves), the rows are made again, the selected preview is read again, and it counts as a change for the pacing (`caught_up(fresh || updated || retry)`). `Stale::shows_in` is as on the trunk before: the implementer's commit had it call an answer fresh when it listed the same items in the same order with another size or date, which a saved file's answer often isn't (review_fixes, the first). docs/manual.md: the "Open folders refresh on their own" paragraph (two sentences), the Refresh row, the filter paragraph.
changelog: A Nushell filter kept its answer for an item after the item had changed. A file that another program saved stayed hidden when it had grown past `size > 10kb`, and stayed listed, and counted in the status bar, when it had shrunk under it. In a folder opened with a filter already on, the folders were judged before their sizes were known, so `size > 100mb` listed none of them, and a comparison joined to another condition, such as `kind == Folder and size > 1mb`, left a Nushell error over an unfiltered list. Refresh (Cmd+R) changed none of it. A filter now runs again when an item comes back with another size or date, and Refresh runs it again in any case, as a filter that goes by the time of day needs.
behaviour_changes: With a Nushell filter on, the filter runs again when an item comes back with another size or date, not only when items come, go or change order. In a folder that is after any reread: the two-second look after another program saved a file under another name that took the file's, Refresh, a file operation here or in another tab, a folder open in place in the list. The list and the status bar's "N of M items pass the filter" follow, and "No Items Pass the Filter" goes when an item passes. Tested (size, date alone, the status count, the message), pictured (review-two-files-saved), and probed with a folder open in place and in the column view (the first column follows; the other columns were never filtered).

A folder opened with a filter already on (also by Back, Forward, Enclosing Folder): its folders are judged again once the index has given their sizes. `size > 100mb` lists the big ones, and `kind == Folder and size > 1mb` no longer leaves a Nushell error over an unfiltered list. Tested, pictured (review-big-folder-listed: `size > 100b` lists atlas at 191 bytes and not beacon at 96; review-folder-opened-under-filter: no error). By reading, the same goes whenever folder sizes come or go later: Calculate All Sizes switched, the list's columns changed, the index finishing a scan.

Refresh (Cmd+R, F5, the menus) runs the filter again in every case, also when every item comes back as it was, which is what a filter that goes by the time of day or by a file's contents needs. The answer before stays in force until the new one is in. Tested, and probed during a search (one run). By reading, it also runs a filter again whose last run ended in an error or the 10 s timeout.

Items that come back as they were start no run, however often the folder is looked at or read. Tested, and counted in review with a stand-in `nu` that notes each run: 5 looks, a quiet reread, each of the four views chosen in turn, and Show Hidden Files switched in a folder without hidden files start none.

Cost, new: opening a folder that holds folders the index has sizes for, with a filter on, starts two `nu` runs where it started one (counted: 2 for each of going there, Back and Forward). A folder whose files are saved again and again runs the filter at each reread, at most every two seconds, where it ran only when items came or went. While "No Items Pass the Filter" is up, such a run shows placeholders for its length, as a run for an item that came or went already did.

Recents: read again and coming out in the same order, it now shows a file's new size and date and reads the selected file's preview again; before, that answer was dropped. It counts as a change for the pacing, so the saves after it show as soon. Tested with the Preview Pane on.

Search by name, a Smart Folder's too: when the search runs again quietly and its answer isn't shown (the reported files make no difference to the list), the rows on screen still take the size and date the answer has for their items, and the selected item's preview is read again. No row comes, goes or moves by it: a saved file that a new search would list first among the matches as good as it stays where it was listed. That holds when the answer is the list on screen, the same items in another order, or a list with a match in it that no report was of, and after a rescan. Tested (a lone result; the older of two equal matches; with an unreported match in the answer; after a rescan). On the trunk before, such an answer was dropped whole.

Such an update counts as a change for how closely the search is followed: a file saved three times shows each time within two looks (tested), while answers that have every item as its row shows it hold the search back as before (tested: after two of them the next save shows at the fourth look).
With the results sorted by Date Modified or Size, a row that was brought up to date moves to where the sort puts it, and stays selected (probed by date). In relevance order it stays where it was.

With a Nushell filter on, a result brought up to date is judged again: probed with a search for roadmap under `size > 10b`, where the match joins the list when saved at 20 bytes and leaves it when saved at 4.
A name being edited among the results keeps its field when its row is brought up to date, and Return renames the file (probed).

By reading only: after a result was renamed in the window its row has the disk's exact date, where an answer has the index's date in whole seconds, so the next quiet answer brings that row up to date once and the selected item's preview is read once more.

A folder among the results has its date read from the disk at each answer. While files come and go in it, each quiet rerun shows its new date and so counts as a change: the search is not held back, and runs again at each look without news, every half minute while files keep coming (probed: a file made and removed in the listed folder every other look showed at every other look, for as long as it went on).
Unchanged: what makes Recents or a search be made again; contents searches; a file written over in place in a folder until Refresh; Return in the filter field with the same text.

docs/manual.md: the filter paragraph says when the filter runs again and what Refresh does; the Refresh row names the filter; the window paragraph says that results which stay as they are show a saved file's new size and date though a save alone doesn't run the search, and that Recents' first file keeps the size and date it showed until Recents is read again.
left_out: The usual quick save, which the watcher reports as a write to the file: a name search that lists the file still does not run again for it, and Recents is still not read for its first file being written to. The row keeps its size and date until the list is next made. Probed in review with a real watcher: a draft renamed over the file at once is counted as one write (the engine's counts went from (2, 2) to (2, 3)) and the result's row stayed; a draft that was there for a second and a half is counted as a file that came and one renamed, and the result showed within two looks. The brief records this as known and not its subject, and the manual says so in both sentences. Reading Recents once the writing to its first file has stopped would close it there, and is pinned the other way by recents_follows_the_files_that_are_written_to ("Written to again it stays first, so Recents isn't read again").
Return in the filter field with unchanged text still does not run the filter again (`set_filter` returns early). The brief asks for Refresh "at the least".
filter-stale-keep-set: not touched. `apply_filter_to`'s exemption for a name being edited and `listed_len` are as new-item-in-hidden-row left them.

The first of the two runs that opening a folder under a filter now starts is not avoided. When the sizes arrive before `nu` answers, as they should in the app, its answer is dropped unseen; when they arrive later (app sizes added up from the disk), the first answer shows until the second.
A row's git status is not part of what is compared: a result or a file in Recents is brought up to date when its size or date differs, and its git badge with it, not for the badge alone.

A file saved at the size it had within the second it was last saved in has, in the index, the size and date it had: Recents and a search's rows don't show such a save (a folder's rows have the disk's exact date).

No picture of the Recents and search half: the screenshot example's index doesn't watch its folder. It was run in headless tests, where `reindex` and `report_change` stand in for the watcher, and in one probe with a real watcher.
`cargo clippy --features term` not run: nothing in src/term calls what changed and no signature it calls changed. Nothing compiled for macOS or Windows; no cfg-gated code is touched.

review_fixes: Found with a probe and fixed: in a search's results, a saved file mostly kept its old row all the same. The implementer's commit showed a quiet answer that the reports don't account for only when it listed the same items in the same order with another size or date (a branch at the top of `Stale::shows_in`, as the brief proposed). The engine lists the matches of one score newest first (`by_rank`), so a file that is saved moves ahead of the matches as good as it, and the answer after a save is the same items in another order unless the file was alone in its score or the newest already. Probed on the implementer's commit with two files, plan one.md and plan two.md, and a search for plan: the older one saved, its row kept "6 bytes" and the pane its old text, through later saves too, until Refresh. Fix: `shows_in` is back to the trunk's text, and `start_search`'s answer, when it isn't shown, brings the rows on screen up to date by path (`show_as_found`), makes the rows again when one changed, reads the selected preview again and counts that as a change for the pacing. The list and its order stay, which is what the rule in `shows_in` is for. It also covers an answer that differs by a match no report was of. Test: a_saved_file_shows_as_it_is_now_in_results_that_stay_as_they_were, seen failing on the implementer's commit.

No kept test said that an answer which changes no row is still one that came out as it was: the tests of the backoff all have a match in the answer that isn't on screen. Its last comment was reworded to stand after the new block.
A test renamed: a_filter_runs_again_for_a_file_saved_at_the_size_it_had, from ..._saved_as_long_as_it_was, which read as "provided that".

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt someone, and what the code and the probes say. (1) A filter that runs over and over, each run a `nu` process, with the list flickering. A run starts only from `apply_filter_to`, when the rows' paths, order, sizes or dates differ from those of the last run, or after Refresh. Rows are made from the listing, the folder sizes read with it, or a search's results, none of which changes between two rebuilds unless something was read again; last-opened dates are not compared, so reading a file for its preview starts nothing. Counted: nothing for looks, quiet rereads, the views; two for a folder opened; one for a save, for a sort, for Refresh. What is left is a folder whose items really change at every reread: one run every two seconds at most. (2) Results or Recents moving under the hands, or the selection, the scroll or a name being edited lost to a quiet update. A search's rows are replaced in place by path; none comes, goes or moves unless the results are sorted by the date or size that changed. The selection goes by path, the scroll isn't touched, and a name's field stays (probed). Recents shows its whole answer, as it did when the order differed. (3) Background work that no longer backs off. A quiet rerun after which a listed row has another size or date counts as a change, so a search that lists a folder files keep coming and going in, or a file that is written to while other matches come and go, runs again at each look without news, or every half minute while they keep coming, where it was held back to once in four minutes. Each such run is one search off the window's thread, one rebuild of the rows, and one `nu` if a filter is on. Answers that change no row still hold it back (tested).

Doubts that remain, for the owner. (a) The pacing in (3): I let it stand because the rows do show something new each time, and a saved file should not show later with each save; the brief proposed to take such rows without counting them as a change. (b) Two `nu` runs for each folder opened under a filter. (c) How little the Recents and search half reaches in the app: a save is mostly reported as a write, which makes neither list be read again (left_out, the first). What this change mends is the answer that was read and thrown away. (d) A row brought up to date stays where it was listed, so until the next search the order is not the one a new search gives (the saved file first among its equals). Refresh shows that one. (e) Only Linux was built and run.

For briefs still to come.
- filter-stale-keep-set: `filter_source` is `Option<Vec<FilterInput>>`, each row's (path, size, modified) in order, and `filter_keep` is still paths. `refresh` sets `filter_source = None` and leaves `filter_keep` in force until the next answer. A folder opened under a filter now has two runs when it holds folders with sizes: over the rows as listed, then over the rows with sizes. When the sizes arrive first, the first run's answer is dropped and the keep-set of the place left stays in force until the second answers, so longer than before by the time the sizes take; when they arrive later, the first answer shows in between. If you tie the keep-set to the rows it answered for, tie it by path: an answer for a file at its old size is applied to the file at its new size until the run for that lands, by design (the answer before stays in force), and a_filter_runs_again_for_a_file_that_was_saved goes by the end state only. With "No Items Pass the Filter" up, the message now also gives way to placeholders for a run started by a changed size or date and by Refresh. refresh_runs_the_filter_again says when no run may start (two looks, a quiet reread).
- files-changed-off-thread: `files_changed` still does `results.retain(exists)`. A quiet answer that isn't shown now writes to `this.results` too (`show_as_found` replaces rows by path), in the same update as its `search_gen` check.
- recents-walk-index: `reload_recents` shows the list when any row's path, size or date differs, or the order does. `recents()` has to give the same size and date for the same file from one read to the next, or Recents is shown, rebuilt and never held back at every read. recents_follows_the_files_that_are_written_to still pins that an answer as it was holds Recents back.
- idle-redraw-after-search, search-start-no-flash: a quiet answer that isn't shown may now make the rows again and notify, only when a row's size or date changed. `searching` stays false and `search_stats` is not replaced by it.
- select-all-perf: with a filter on, `apply_filter_to` builds a Vec of (PathBuf, size, modified) for the rows at each `rebuild_rows`, where it built a Vec of paths.
- multi-word-highlights, content-match-highlight: a row that `show_as_found` replaces is the answer's row, with the answer's highlights and git status. A contents search is never run again quietly, so its rows are never replaced this way.
- query-history-boost, near-miss-beside-scattered, fix-folder-search-own-name-pool, accented-names-search: `show_as_found` compares `entry.size` and `entry.modified` of the row on screen with the answer's row at the same path. If two answers to one search ever give another size or date for a file that didn't change (one reading the disk, one the index), every quiet rerun counts as a change: the rows are made again each time and the search is never held back. A change of rank alone moves no row on screen until an answer is shown whole.
- regex-content-search, adhoc-index-feedback: `start_search`'s answer has one more step between `fresh` and the early return for an answer that isn't shown (`updated`); a contents search never gets there, since only a quiet search has `stale`.
- restore-session-tabs: each tab follows its own search and filter; a tab with a filter on runs `nu` again when its rows come back with other sizes or dates, whether it shows or not.
- fix-wording-after-later-changes: sentences of the manual that are new or changed here: "If it made none, the list stays as it is, and a file in it that was saved since shows with its new size and date, though a save alone doesn't make the search run again."; "... with the size and date it showed until Recents is read again."; the Refresh row ends "and re-runs the search and the filter"; the filter paragraph's second and third sentences.
- fix-rename-press-selection, view-switch-keeps-selection, split-active-pane: nothing here changes when rows are made after an edit or a view switch. Choosing another view starts no filter run unless the rows differ (the list with a folder open in place). Refresh in a pane forgets that pane's `filter_source` only.
